chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a woman who enters Mecca performing Tamattu' Hajj and menstruates before she becomes free (from Ihram); when does her Tamattu' status end? He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The fading of the sun on the Day of Tawreeyah. And Musa (peace be upon him) said: The morning prayer on the Day of Tawreeyah. I said: May I be your ransom, most of your followers enter on the Day of Tawreeyah, perform Tawaf and Sa'i, then enter Ihram for Hajj. He said: The fading of the sun. I mentioned to him the narration of Ajlan, Abu Salih, and he said: No. When the sun fades, the Tamattu' ends. I said: Then is she still in her Ihram, or does she renew her Ihram for Hajj? He said: No, and she remains in her Ihram. I said: Then is there a sacrifice (Hady) upon her? He said: No, unless she wishes to volunteer (for an extra sacrifice). Then he said: As for us, when we see the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah before we enter Ihram, the Tamattu' has passed us by.

key_terms.مُتَمِّعَةً: Performing Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tawreeyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: When does a woman's Tamattu' Hajj status end if she menstruates before completing the final Tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the precise moment the 'Tamattu' status expires for a woman who menstruates before completing the Tawaf al-Ifadah, with Imam al-Rida (AS) affirming the view of Abu Ja'far (AS) that it ends at sunset on the Day of Tawreeyah. It resolves the legal nuance that she remains in her original Ihram without needing to renew it or offering a mandatory sacrifice, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt. The narration also notes the Imams' personal practice of considering the Tamattu' invalid if the new moon of Dhul-Hijjah is sighted before they enter Ihram.
